headline: What Hyderabad has been promised about its water
intro: Dated, public undertakings about Hyderabad's water, each with the citation that records it. A status only changes here when a dated citation supports the change - not when a deadline passes quietly, and not on the basis of a press release restating an old target as a new one. Where a promise involves a number we have been unable to source from the promising authority, that is said in the entry rather than smoothed over.

status_legend.on-track: Evidence of progress against the stated date, from a dated source
status_legend.overdue: The stated date has passed without a dated source recording completion
status_legend.unverifiable: The commitment is public and dated, but no public instrument reports progress against it
status_legend.superseded: Replaced or restated by a later commitment

commitments.title: Musi Riverfront Development, Phase I
commitments.committed_by: Government of Telangana / Musi Riverfront Development Corporation
commitments.what: Rejuvenation of a 55 km stretch of the Musi from Gandipet to Gowrelly, championed by Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy. In May 2026 the state released Rs 375 crore as the first instalment against Rs 1,500 crore earmarked in the 2026-27 budget, and the Chief Secretary inspected Phase I progress. The programme's headline cost has been reported at around Rs 7,000 crore, which we record as reported rather than as an established figure.

commitment_source.label: Telangana releases Rs 375 crore first instalment for Musi Riverfront Phase I, against Rs 1,500 crore in the 2026-27 budget

status_history.note: Funds released and progress inspected, but no published completion date for Phase I and no public milestone schedule to measure against. Recorded as unverifiable rather than on-track: money moving is not the same as a deadline being met.

commitments.note: The riverfront programme is the single largest thing being done to the Musi and the hardest to hold to account, because no dated deliverable has been published. A phase-wise milestone schedule is the document to ask for.

commitments.title: Intercept and treat all sewage entering the Musi along the 34 km Bapu Ghat to Gowrelly stretch
commitments.what: Interception and diversion of sewage outfalls before they reach the river, along a 34 km reach, as the sewage-side counterpart to the riverfront works. This is the load-bearing claim in every Musi cleanup plan: without interception, riverfront construction changes the banks and not the water.

commitment_source.label: The Hans India - Musi makeover: sewage interception and decentralised treatment

status_history.note: No public reporting of how many outfalls along the 34 km reach have actually been intercepted. The count of trapped-versus-remaining outfalls is the verification instrument, and it is not published.

commitments.note: Delhi's equivalent commitment - trapping 39 drains to the Yamuna - is trackable because the trapped count is reported. Hyderabad's is not.

commitments.title: 39 new sewage treatment plants along the Musi under AMRUT
commitments.committed_by: HMWSSB, under the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation
commitments.what: 39 STPs totalling a reported 972 MLD, described as progressing under AMRUT, on top of an existing estate and a further tranche said to be already commissioned.

commitment_source.label: Construction World - Hyderabad's Musi river revitalised (STP programme figures)

status_history.note: PLANT COUNTS AND CAPACITIES ARE NOT USED AS FACT ANYWHERE ON THIS SITE. Published figures for Hyderabad's STP estate are mutually inconsistent across sources - variously 25 plants at 772 MLD, 27 commissioned at 1,106 MLD, 39 under AMRUT at 972 MLD, and a total estate of 45 plants at 1,878 MLD. The commitment is recorded because it was publicly made; the numbers are quoted as reported and are not reconciled. HMWSSB's RTI 4(1)(b) disclosure or an annual report is the document that would settle it.

commitments.note: The clearest example on this page of why the site refuses to publish a headline treatment-capacity number for Hyderabad.

commitments.title: HYDRAA to restore 10 lakes a year, toward 200 rejuvenated lakes
commitments.committed_by: Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA)
commitments.what: A stated target of ten lake restorations a year against a vision of 200 restored lakes. Six lakes completed in Phase I, 14 under restoration in Phase II, and four more begun on 25 June with bhoomi puja at Ibrahim Pedda Cheruvu (Rajendranagar), Bhagirathamma Cheruvu (Gandipet), Kamuni Cheruvu (Moosapet) and Kapra Cheruvu (Medchal-Malkajgiri).

commitment_source.label: The Week - HYDRAA reshapes Hyderabad through lake restoration and land protection

status_history.note: Six completed in Phase I and 14 in progress in Phase II, against a stated ten a year - named lakes and dated bhoomi pujas make this one of the few Hyderabad commitments with a verifiable trail.

commitments.note: At ten a year, 200 lakes takes twenty years - and the metropolitan register holds 2,978. Worth stating the ratio plainly alongside the progress.

commitments.title: Complete the gazetted Full Tank Level notifications for the region's lakes
commitments.what: Every lake is meant to receive a preliminary FTL notification and then a final one after objections. All 2,978 lakes in the register have the preliminary; 1,352 have the final, leaving 1,626 without a legally settled boundary.

commitment_source.label: HMDA gazetted lake register (the register is itself the record of progress)

status_history.note: Final notifications ran at 152 in 2016 then effectively stopped - 10, 60, 2, 3 and 2 across 2017-2023. Then 533 in 2024, 533 in 2025 and 57 so far in 2026: two-thirds of every final notification ever issued arrived in the last two years. Directly measurable from the register, which is why this entry can carry a status the others cannot.

commitments.note: The one Hyderabad commitment we can audit continuously, because the promising authority publishes the register that records it. Rangareddy remains the laggard at 34.5% finally notified against 68.0% in Siddipet.

commitments.title: Hold elections to the three new municipal corporations
commitments.committed_by: Telangana State Election Commission / Government of Telangana
commitments.what: Elections to seven municipal corporations and 116 municipalities were held on 11 February 2026, but the three Hyderabad corporations - GHMC, Cyberabad and Malkajgiri - were deferred to a later date following the trifurcation. Until they are held the corporations are administered by a Special Officer and there are no elected councillors.

commitment_source.label: Telangana municipal elections held 11 February 2026; GHMC and two other corporations deferred

status_history.note: No polling date announced for the three Hyderabad corporations as of this compilation. Recorded because it is the reason the ward-representative surface on this site is empty rather than incomplete.

commitments.note: Directly relevant to water accountability: 300 wards were gazetted in December 2025 and nobody has yet been elected to any of them.

commitments.title: Publish the encroachment count GHMC's own drain layer defines
commitments.committed_by: GHMC (implicit - the schema is published, the data is not)
commitments.what: GHMC's storm-water drain layer defines fields for encroachments per nala, separated into government, private and religious, with a count of cases in court. All five fields are published as zero for all 96 nalas.

commitment_source.label: GHMC nala layer via OpenCity - fields present and uniformly empty, verified 2026-07-26

status_history.note: Not a promise the city made in words, but a disclosure it designed and did not complete. Included because the schema specifies exactly what to request, which makes it the most actionable information gap on this page.

commitments.note: In a city that created an agency to demolish encroachments, a column of zeros is an unfilled field rather than a clean record. Tracked here so the day it is populated is visible.

update_model: Status changes require a dated citation. A deadline passing does not by itself move an entry to 'overdue' unless a due date was publicly stated - most Hyderabad water commitments are announced without one, which is why 'unverifiable' is the most common status on this page rather than a hedge.
sources_note: Several entries rest on news reporting because the underlying government orders and programme schedules are not published. Where a figure is contested across sources - above all the STP counts - the entry says so instead of picking one. Provenance discipline for the whole city is documented in docs/cities/hyderabad/data-sources.md.
